column4: Master-brand listing uses an API key and heterogeneous media metadata without an explicit unrestricted-access policy.
Programme metadata includes embargo and availability fields; API-key authentication does not resolve access restrictions.
Broadcast service metadata has API-key security but no affirmative unrestricted access or caller-policy statement.
Raw episode retrieval includes embargo and publication-rights metadata without a stated object authorization policy.
Order accountId is both a path and response field but its personal-versus-tenant meaning and caller binding remain unspecified.
Order history uses accountId context but only history wrappers in ERD and unknown security.
Changing a marketplace order refers to your order but the only errors column supplies no account ownership lookup.
Webhook id_user is inferred; Administration tag alone does not establish a required admin role.
Review Poster and UserID describe response authorship without a stated owner-only update rule or verified binding.
Summary explicitly forbids reading another owner's recipe, but flattened Poster/UserID and RecipeID in inferred steps do not verify the lookup binding.
Adding a recipe note exposes UserID in response data but neither ownership semantics nor lookup binding is specified.
Cash-payment update has financial identifiers but unknown security and no caller authorization relation.
Customer ledger data includes account fields without identifying the authenticated caller's ownership or tenancy.
Customer opening-balance retrieval has only monetary response fields and unknown authorization.
Payment update includes bank and supplier identifiers but no owner or tenant authorization evidence.
CustomerId and Company in an address response do not prove that the API caller owns that customer record.
Customer-by-id retrieval has no verified subject key or authentication requirements.
Adding a customer address exposes CustomerId but no verified caller-to-customer authorization relation.
Order creation in a Billbee account has flattened buyer and customer data but no defined caller access rule.
Document organization is billing metadata, not verified tenant identity or database lookup evidence.
Document tax-submission status requires an API key but the response has no ownership mapping.
repository:admin is an OAuth permission rather than a proved application role or administrator bypass.
Commit-comment user is inferred authorship metadata; repository scope does not prove owner-only mutation.
Commit report reporter is descriptive and security is unknown, leaving access policy unresolved.
Bulk report-annotation mutation has workspace context but no tenant lookup or explicit role policy.
Commit build-status retrieval has repository authentication alternatives but no specified object authorization.
Transit arrival lookup requires an API key; public-looking transit data alone does not prove unrestricted API access.
Container-group inspection has unknown security and no owner or tenant columns.
Export status includes username and project_slug in the path but no verified caller or tenant binding in job fields.
Collaboration role and created_by fields describe a resource and do not specify the calling user's required role.
Comment created_by identifies possible authorship, not a verified owner-only read policy or lookup.
Enterprise device-pin listing has OAuth security but pagination-only ERD cannot resolve tenant or admin authorization.
Sanctions-report retrieval uses a user key but report ownership is absent from supplied data.
Product provider is supplier metadata rather than a proved tenant field; user-key authentication gives no policy.
Sending SMS uses Basic authentication without a concrete role, membership tier or object-owner requirement.
Webhook update includes contactEmailAddress but no verified ownership relationship or caller policy.
Leaderboard summary references signed-in friends, while membershipType is a game identifier rather than a required subscription tier.
Team-member user retrieval exposes admin flags but neither a verified subject key nor an admin-only policy.
Call-recording retrieval uses Basic authentication without any supplied call owner binding.
NFT owner is blockchain ownership data, not caller authorization, and API security is unknown.
Polygon NFT-owner lookup has unknown API access requirements; on-chain owner does not identify the authorized caller.
Tron account balance query lacks explicit unrestricted-access evidence despite its blockchain resource identifiers.
Conversation creator and tenant fields are inferred; WRITE and MANAGE scopes do not establish admin or owner permissions.
Group-participant removal has OAuth permission scopes but no verified owner or tenant rule.
Message creatorId describes authorship; READ_CONVERSATIONS does not establish owner-only message access.
Conversation-item listing supplies creatorId on items but no caller-to-conversation authorization relation.
Organization update has an inferred id without verified tenant binding or specified security.
Organization addon-provider update has provider metadata but no proved organization authorization rule.
Organization addon-plan listing exposes prices, not required caller membership tiers, and security is unknown.
Organization plan update has no verified tenant lookup or required role evidence.
